plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in a wide range of forms, from pompons to spiders. Widely cultivated in gardens and as cut flowers, it thrives in cool autumn weather and is a staple of fall displays.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia (China and Japan)
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for over 2,500 years, and the flower is the national floral emblem of Japan, where the Chrysanthemum Festival is celebrated each autumn.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that bears fragrant, delicate single or semi-double flowers in late autumn when little else is blooming. It is popular in warm temperate gardens and attracts late-season pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, Australia and New Zealand
plants.funFact: The leaves of Camellia sasanqua can be used to make a tea, and its seeds are pressed to produce a camellia oil used for cooking and cosmetics.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular tree that erupts with clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers before its leaves fully emerge. In spring in the Southern Hemisphere it lines streets and parks, carpeting the ground with fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), Argentina and New Zealand
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, so many jacarandas are planted that the city is nicknamed the Jacaranda City, and a fallen jacaranda flower is said in Australia to bring luck to students before exams.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: A daisy-like annual with feathery foliage and cup-shaped blooms on tall, slender stems. In frost-free regions of the subtropics and in warm autumns it continues to bloom into November, while it is also a spring and summer favorite in the Southern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to late autumn; blooms into November in mild climates
plants.location: Native to Mexico; naturalized and cultivated in warm regions across the Americas, Asia and Australia
plants.funFact: Its name comes from the Greek word kosmos, meaning order or harmony, a reference to its evenly arranged petals.
